task_description: The team must determine, per Wikipedia, which two ASEAN-bloc countries have the greatest great-circle distance between their capital cities, and return them as an alphabetically ordered comma-separated list. The gold answer is 'Indonesia, Myanmar' — i.e. the Jakarta-to-Naypyidaw pair is the farthest among the standard ASEAN capitals, so the correct response reduces to the two countries Indonesia and Myanmar in alphabetical order.
final_vs_expected: produced no FINAL ANSWER (hit the message cap; last published text was 'Myanmar, Timor-Leste') vs gold 'Indonesia, Myanmar' — never finalized, and the working hypothesis was also the wrong pair.
primary_cause: The selector never routed to the Finalizer and instead looped WebResearcher/Analyst around an unmet 'compute all pairs' demand until the 30-message cap, so the run timed out with no FINAL ANSWER (and on a wrong, never-computed pair).
mast_rationale: 1.5 (unaware of termination): the Finalizer role exists to emit 'FINAL ANSWER:' but the selector never picks it; every turn re-selects WebResearcher or Analyst, so the run never terminates and hits the cap (rc=timeout, 900s). 3.2 (no/incomplete verification): the Critic at turn 3 explicitly demanded an actual pairwise distance computation across all ASEAN capitals ('No one actually computed the capital-to-capital distances; the claim that this is the "furthest" pair is asserted, not demonstrated'), but the only run_python ever executed (turn 10) computed a single Naypyidaw->Dili distance (4506 km), never the full pairwise table — the verification the Critic asked for was never carried out. 2.5 (ignored other agent's input): the Critic's concrete request for a full pairwise comparison and for verifying Timor-Leste's membership was acknowledged in words ~6 times but never acted on in substance; the loop just re-states 'not yet proven' without doing it. 1.3 (step repetition): WebResearcher re-fetches the same capital coordinates (Bandar Seri Begawan, Vientiane, Phnom Penh, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur) in turns 6 and 11 that were already gathered in turn 1, with no new synthesis.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: WebResearcher runs a 7-round private loop, searching/fetching Wikipedia coordinates for most ASEAN capitals. It never computes distances rigorously — it does rough mental great-circle estimates ('Manila to Naypyidaw is about 2,760 km', 'Dili to Bangkok is around 4050 km'). In round 7 it suddenly decides Timor-Leste is an ASEAN member and that Dili (far SE) vs Naypyidaw (far NW) is the extreme, and publishes 'Myanmar, Timor-Leste'. Turn 2: Analyst, in one round, does NOT compute anything ('computing the actual distance isn't necessary since the user already gave the answer') and just re-publishes 'Myanmar, Timor-Leste'. Turn 3: Critic correctly flags that nothing was computed, the 'furthest' claim is unproven, no comparison against all pairs exists, and Timor-Leste's membership is unverified; it asks WebResearcher to confirm membership and Analyst to actually compute all pairwise distances. Turns 4-5: selector routes to Analyst, who twice restates the Critic's own objections ('the "furthest" claim is not proved') without computing — pure echo. Turn 6: WebResearcher re-fetches several capital coordinates already in hand, then publishes that it verified coordinates and membership but 'did not complete a full pairwise distance calculation'. Turns 7-9: Analyst three more times says it still needs the full coordinate set / pairwise table, never computing. Turn 10: Analyst finally calls run_python — but only for the single Naypyidaw->Dili pair (4506 km), not the pairwise sweep the Critic demanded; still concludes 'not yet proven'. Turns 11-19: selector ping-pongs WebResearcher (mostly re-fetching the same coords or publishing a bare 'Myanmar, Timor-Leste', once even an empty message) while the Finalizer is never selected. The run exhausts the message cap at turn 19+ with no FINAL ANSWER.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is primarily a structural-nonconvergence + broken-verification failure, with a single-agent capability error underneath, and only weak genuine inter-agent misalignment. (1) Capability root: WebResearcher never did the systematic computation the task requires. It eyeballed great-circle distances in its head and latched onto Timor-Leste/Dili as the SE extreme. The actual gold pair is Indonesia (Jakarta, ~6.2 S 106.8 E) and Myanmar (Naypyidaw); if the question scopes to the original 10 ASEAN members (no Timor-Leste, which only acceded in principle), Dili is excluded and Jakarta-Naypyidaw wins. The team both (a) mis-scoped membership and (b) never computed, so it would have been wrong even had it finalized. (2) Verification theater / non-convergence is the proximate cause of the no_answer outcome: the Critic asked exactly the right question (do the full pairwise comparison), everyone verbally agreed it was needed, but the one computation performed answered a different question (one pair, not all pairs). Nobody ever produced the full coordinate table + all-pairs argmax, so the precondition the team set for itself was never met, and the selector — apparently treating 'unmet Critic request' as 'not done, keep researching/analyzing' — never advanced to Finalizer. (3) Selector misrouting: across ~19 turns the selector alternated WebResearcher/Analyst and never once chose Finalizer, even when WebResearcher was just repeating the answer string; its reasoning each turn re-derives 'we still need the full pairwise list' (turn 16/17/19) and routes back into the loop, the classic re-pick-forever pattern that burns the cap.
reasoning_vs_published: The private-vs-published gap is mild here; the more telling divergence is reasoning-vs-action and ignored-input. (a) Turn 2 Analyst reasoning: 'computing the actual distance isn't necessary since the user already gave the answer' — yet its published role is to compute. It then spends turns 4-10 publishing that the computation IS necessary, never reconciling. (b) The Critic's published correction at turn 3 ('No one actually computed the capital-to-capital distances; the claim ... is asserted, not demonstrated' and 'Analyst: actually compute the pairwise capital distances across the ASEAN set') is acknowledged in nearly every later Analyst message ('the full pairwise comparison is missing') but never substantively executed — input received, paraphrased, and dropped (2.5). (c) Turn 10 Analyst privately runs run_python for ONLY the Naypyidaw->Dili pair (result 4506 km) then publishes 'the key missing piece is still the full pairwise comparison' — i.e. it recognizes its own computation did not satisfy the requirement, yet does not do the larger computation it just admitted is needed (reasoning-action mismatch, weak 2.6). (d) WebResearcher's turn-1 round-7 reasoning shows the capability slip privately ('Dili to Bangkok is around 4050 km, which may actually be farther') — rough estimates, never verified — and this never improves; later publishes degrade to a bare 'Myanmar, Timor-Leste' with the evidence stripped (unreflective publishing). No information was maliciously withheld; the team simply never generated the evidence and never finalized.
